operational-example.copy: Collect a support or assistant message with visible label, controlled value, send action, optional attachment, and recoverable validation.

rationale: Avoids local visual or workflow duplication.

items.rule: Composes Surface as the form boundary without creating a Card shell.
Composes Text Area and Field Action for multiline input and helper/error copy.
Composes Button and blocks empty or disabled submission.
Optional Icon Button for governed attachment behavior.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled > sending > error > focus > filled > default
items: Keep visible labels and accessible names aligned.
Expose machine-readable state through props and data attributes.
Do not rely on color, symbol, or placeholder text alone.
Preserve keyboard, focus, disabled, loading, and recovery behavior.

variants.copy: chat-composer variants stay semantic and do not fork visual contracts.

states.copy: Chat Composer states preserve the shared Field, Message, Surface, Button, and State cascade while keeping message entry controlled or uncontrolled.

demos.label: Filled
demos.value: Can you review this card limit?

api-foundations.copy: chat-composer API exposes semantic props while Flow foundations own state, density, tone, frame, and accessibility.

props.name: sending
props.notes: Locks the composer while submit is in progress.

props.name: onValueChange
props.notes: Controlled value callback with metadata and event.

do: Use Chat Composer for one conversational message entry.
Use when controlled/uncontrolled value, sending state, and send callback must be explicit.
Use inside a formal conversational pattern or template, not as a standalone chat workflow.
dont: The flow needs full thread orchestration, escalation, or channel routing.
The message contains regulated or irreversible content.
A custom textarea, fake send button, or local attachment shell is requested.
items: Confirm symbols and tone have visible text fallback.
